messages.subject: basic question - residual covariance matrix
parts:
Dear community,

I want to compute the residual covariance matrix manually, but I think I am doing something wrong.
Suppose that this is my model:

my.model <- '
# Measurement model
Y1 =~ 1 * y1
Y2 =~ 1 * y2
Y3 =~ 1 * y3

# measurement error
y1 ~~ 0.10 * y1
y2 ~~ 0.02 * y2
y3 ~~ 0.05 * y3

# structural model
Y1 ~ x1 + x2
Y2 ~ x3 + x4
Y3 ~ Y1 + Y2

# error variance
Y1 ~~ Y2
'
my.fit <- sem(my.model, fixed.x = TRUE, data = data)
 
x1 to x4 are deterministic variables, so they have not variance and phi is zero. The data is "y1", "y2", "y3", "x1", "x2", "x3", "x4". All variables were standardized.
Now I want to see the residual covariance matrix of the endogenous variables (Y1, Y2, Y3), so:

B <- inspect(my.fit, "est")$beta[1:3,1:3] # beta coefficients
I <- diag(nrow = 3, ncol = 3) # lambda_y coefficients
A <- inspect(my.fit, "est")$beta[1:3,4:7] # gamma coefficients
V <- inspect(my.fit.lv.ML, "est")$psi[1:3,1:3] # Psi coefficients
Th <- inspect(my.fit.lv.ML, "est")$theta[1:3,1:3] #theta coefficients
IB <- solve(I - B)

SigmaHat <- (IB %*% V %*% t(IB)) + Th
S <- cov(data[,1:3])
Residuals <- S - SigmaHat

Why Residuals is not equal to residuals(my.fit, "raw")$cov[1:3,1:3]?

Thanks in advance,

Marcos

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: basic question - residual covariance matrix
parts:
Marcos--
     Which residual covariance matrix do you want? "psi" IS the residual covariance matrix for the "factors" (Y1, Y2, Y3) while "theta" IS the residual covariance matrix for the observed variables y1, y2, y3. You have specified the residual variances for y1, y2, y3 by assignment. At the same time, you specified that Y1, Y2, Y3 are not strictly equivalent to y1, y2, y3.
--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: basic question - residual covariance matrix
parts: > Why Residuals is not equal to residuals(my.fit, "raw")$cov[1:3,1:3]?

Two things: you need the full matrices, including the x's (not just the
first three rows/cols), and S is divided by N (not N-1):

attach(inspect(my.fit, "est"))
IB.inv <- solve(diag( nrow(beta) ) - beta)
Sigma.hat <- lambda %*% IB.inv %*% psi %*% t(IB.inv) %*% t(lambda) + theta
# should be the same as fitted(my.fit)$cov

# sample cov (divided by N, instead of N-1)
S <- cov(Data[,lavNames(my.fit)]) * (nobs(my.fit) - 1) / nobs(my.fit)

# residuals
Sigma.hat - S
# resid(my.fit)$cov

Yves.

Dear Ed and Yves,

I have one more question about this topic. In the example that I provided Xs are deterministic variables ( ξ ~ N( ζ,0) ), so I set fixed.x = TRUE in the sem() function. However, when you estimate Sigma.hat you consider Xs as random variables, as phi (which are the values for Xs in psi lavaan matrix) is not zero. Please, could you explain why is that?

I leave a small example that anyone can reproduce

library(lavaan)
rm(list=ls())
x <- rnorm(1000,1,1)
y <- 0.5*x + rnorm(1000,0.1,1)
z <- 1.2*x + rnorm(1000,0.1,1)
d <- data.frame(x=x,y=y,z=z)

model <- '
y ~ x
z ~ x
y ~~ 0 * z
'
my.fit <- sem(model, data = d, meanstructure = F, fixed.x = T)
summary(my.fit)

attach(inspect(my.fit, "est"))
beta
lambda
psi # here, if x is deterministic (fixed.x=T), should x ~~ x equal zero?
theta
IB.inv <- solve(diag( nrow(beta) ) - beta)
IB.inv
Sigma.hat <- lambda %*% IB.inv %*% psi %*% t(IB.inv) %*% t(lambda) + theta

Sigma.hat

I really appreciate hour help.
Kind regards,
Marcos

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: basic question - residual covariance matrix
parts:
On 06/07/2016 04:25 PM, Marcos Angelini wrote:
> Dear Ed and Yves,
>
> I have one more question about this topic. In the example that I
> provided Xs are deterministic variables ( ξ ~ N( ζ,0) ), so I set
> fixed.x = TRUE in the sem() function. However, when you estimate
> Sigma.hat you consider Xs as random variables
No, we do not.

as phi (which are the
> values for Xs in psi lavaan matrix) is not zero.

The values in psi simply reflect the observed (sample)
variance/covariance values of the 'fixed.x' covariates.

Compare:

> psi
y z x
y 0.99
z 0.00 1.00
x 0.00 0.00 0.95

and

> round(cov(d[,c("y","z","x")]), 2)
y z x
y 1.28 0.60 0.52
z 0.60 2.39 1.15
x 0.52 1.15 0.95

0.95 is simply the sample-based variance of x.

Look also at the parameter table:

> parTable(my.fit)
id lhs op rhs user group free ustart exo label plabel start est se
1 1 y ~ x 1 1 1 NA 0 .p1. 0.000 0.550 0.032
2 2 z ~ x 1 1 2 NA 0 .p2. 0.000 1.206 0.032
3 3 y ~~ z 1 1 0 0 0 .p3. 0.000 0.000 0.000
4 4 y ~~ y 0 1 3 NA 0 .p4. 0.639 0.990 0.044
5 5 z ~~ z 0 1 4 NA 0 .p5. 1.191 1.000 0.045
6 6 x ~~ x 0 1 0 NA 1 .p6. 0.950 0.950 0.000


where you can see (last line) that 'x ~~ x' is an 'exogenous' variance,
not free, but fixed to its starting value: 0.950

Yves.
